It is submitted that the appellant has been convicted under Section 366 of I.P.C. with five years R.I. and a fine of Rs. 5,000/- with default stipulation of six months R.I.

He is also convicted under Section 376 (3) of I.P.C. with twenty years R.I. and a fine of Rs. 10,000/- with default stipulation of one year R.I.
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the prosecution story in short is that the father of the prosecutrix stated that on 18/03/2019 after having his dinner, he had gone for securing his fields.
At about 9:00 P.M., NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17599 2 CRA-8175-2023 his wife talked with him on her mobile phone and informed him that the prosecutrix is not at home.

He immediately came back to the home and looked for the prosecutrix in his neighbourhood and village but when no trace was available, then he along with his wife lodged a report at Shahpur against unknown persons.

On his report, the Police Station Shahpur has registered Crime No.
204/2019 under Section 363 of I.P.C. and had also separately registered missing person report 07/19 as contained in Ex. P-5.

sentences.text: On being traced, the prosecutrix stated that on 18/03/2019 at about 9:00 P.M. when she was standing outside her home, then accused Kanhaiya on a promise to marry had taken to Pune (Maharashtra) where they got a room in Maharashtra and the appellant violated her privacy against her will.
The appellant had taken her to Wapi from Maharashtra and they roam around in Gujarat where they established relationship like husband and wife.
On recording statements of the prosecutrix under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., the appellant was arrested.
Both the appellant and the prosecutrix were subjected to medical examination.
Samples were sent for F.S.L. investigation.
After investigation, a chargesheet was filed.
The appellant abjured his guilt.

The trial was conducted and,
thereafter, he has been convicted under Section 366 and 376 (3) of I.P.C. with the sentences as mentioned above.

5. The learned trial court has referred to Dakhil Kharij Register Ex. P-8 (c) in which date of birth of the prosecutrix is mentioned as 14/05/2004 and date of admission is mentioned as 13/07/2009 in the first class.
The prosecutrix had taken transfer certificate from the school on 1/05/2015 after passing Vth NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17599 3 CRA-8175-2023 class.

Thereafter,
there is a school certificate issued by Headmaster of the school contained in Ex. P-9 certifying her date of birth to be 14th May, 2004.

6. It is submitted that in the medical examination Ex. P-11, it is mentioned that a "A boy called named Kaniya Yadav age-24 years leaving with her for 4 months there they got married and leaving them at Gujarat and came on 29/06/2019 at morning."
On examination, it was found that hymen was old ruptured.
There were no symptoms or injury seen on the internal or external parts of the body.
The Doctor had sealed the vaginal slide, pubic hair brown colour panty etc. and had given to the Constable and had mentioned that no definite opinion can be given regarding commission of rape.
This Ex. P-1 has been proved by PW-6 Dr. Surbhi.

7. The D.N.A. report which is available on record but has not been exhibited reveals that the Y-chromosome stain found on the panty of the prosecutrix match with the Y-chromosome STR DNA profile obtained from the blood sample of the appellant and all the genetic markers contain similar allele.

8. Now, the question is two fold as to what was the age of the prosecutrix at the time of the incident and secondly whether it is a case of consent between two adults or violation of privacy of the minor.
9. PW-1 is the mother of the prosecutrix.
She has stated that the prosecutrix has studied upto IXth class in a village school.
The incident took place around Holi Festival.
After four months of elopement, the prosecutrix was recovered by Police Station Shahpur wherefrom, she was recovered is not known to her.

This witness was declared hostile when she stated that she NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17599 4 CRA-8175-2023 cannot say that as to whether any serious incident had taken place with her daughter or not ?
10.
In the cross-examination, this witness has admitted that she had not gone to admit the prosecutrix in the school.
She further admitted that the prosecutrix was admitted by her husband.
She further admitted that her husband had recorded date of birth of the prosecutrix on his own.

She admitted that on 18/09/2019, she had gone to Wapi in connection with making of bricks and at that time, her age was more than 18 years.
13. PW-3 father of the prosecutrix admitted that Kanhaiya is brother-in- law in relationship.
In para 8, this witness has stated that date of birth of the prosecutrix is not known to him.
The school master has recorded the date of birth on his own volition.

He admitted that until and unless the girls attain the age of 18 years or 20-21 years, their marriage is not performed.

sentences.text: It is crystal clear that the prosecution has failed to discharge its burden to prove the age of the prosecutrix to be minor and once, that burden is not discharged either by the prosecution by examining father of the prosecutrix or school master of the school from where she had taken admission, it cannot be said that in terms of Section 35 of the Evidence Act, the prosecution has proved the age of the prosecutrix to be major.

16. When these facts are taken into consideration and also the statement of the prosecutrix that she had gone with the appellant on her own volition, there was no force or coercion on her, they had established relationship as husband and wife on their own will and they lived together, then in the absence of the prosecution proving her to be minor, none of the ingredients of Section 35 are proved and when the age of the prosecutrix becomes doubtful; then in the light of the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case o f Birad Mal Singhvi Vs. Anand Purohit AIR 1988 SC 1796 wherein in para-15, it is mentioned as under :-
The High Court held that in view of the entries contained in the Ex. 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 proved by Anantram Sharma PW 3 and Kailash Chandra Taparia PW 5, the date of birth of Hukmichand and Suraj Prakash Joshi was proved and on that assumption it held NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17599 7 CRA-8175-2023 that the two candidates had attained more than 25 years of age on the date of their nomination.

entities.text: Birad Mal Singhvi Vs. Anand Purohit AIR 1988 SC 1796
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our opinion the High Court committed serious error.

Section 35 of the Indian Evidence Act lays down that entry in any public, official book, register, record stating a fact in issue or relevant fact and made by a public servant in the discharge of his official duty specially enjoined by the law of the country is itself the relevant fact.

An entry relating to date of birth made in the school register is relevant and admissible under Section 35 of the Act but the entry regarding to the age of a person in a school register is of not much evidentiary value to prove the age of the person in the absence of the material on which the age was recorded.

In Raja Janaki Nath Roy & Ors. v. Jyotish Chandra Acharya Chowdhury, AIR 1941 CAL. 41 a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court discarded the entry in school register about the age of a party to the suit on the ground that there was no evidence to show on what material the entry in the register about the age of the plaintiff was made.

register or record, secondly, it must be an entry stating a fact in issue or relevant fact;
